//: This corpus was built to test a hypothesis, and the run disproved it. Both statements below
are measurements, not expectations, and the file is kept because the negative one is useful.
THE HYPOTHESIS. `corpus_ts` reports both LSP arms as `n/a — 6 unanswered`, and bench/README.md
explains that by its missing tsconfig: without a project file `tsserver` treats every file as
its own inferred project, cannot see across files, and returns an empty reference list. If that
were the cause for the two class-qualified targets, a typed copy would unblock them, and the
readiness ledger's last technical item — tighten class-qualified method resolution — would
have a measurable candidate fix: ask the language server, which resolves a receiver by type.
WHAT WAS MEASURED. It is not the cause for that shape. With and without this file, byte-identical
sources, `--op symbol --engine lsp --target StrategyChain.resolve` returns the same thing:
## Symbol: StrategyChain.resolve
## References — not retrieved
> the symbol's file path was not resolved, so references were never requested.
The failure is one step earlier than the tsconfig can reach. `providers/lsp.py`'s
`_split_target_file_hint` returns early on any target without an `@file` hint, so the dotted
name goes to Serena verbatim — and Serena name paths are SLASH-separated. Probed directly:
`find_symbol("StrategyChain.resolve")` → `[]`; `find_symbol("StrategyChain/resolve")` →
`{name_path: "StrategyChain/resolve", relative_path: "src/strategyChain.ts", lines 12-14}`.
The dot→slash conversion already exists in that same function, three lines below the early
return, reachable only when a file hint is present.
WHY THIS TREE IS STILL HERE. The fix belongs in `lsp.py`, and when it lands it needs a tree to
be measured on. This is that tree: the class-qualified pair isolated, oracle coverage 100%, and
a project file present so that the inferred-project confound bench/README.md documents cannot
be the explanation for whatever the LSP arm reports next. It removes a candidate confound that
turned out not to be the operative one — which is worth keeping, and is not what this file was
originally claimed to do.
Deliberately minimal: no `paths`, no `baseUrl`. Every import in these five files is relative,
and an alias map would add a variable to a tree whose value is having almost none.
